articles.title: Russia orders Apple to surrender users' messages on demand
articles.description: Apple and Microsoft have been added to a Russian state surveillance registry, requiring them to hand over users' text, video and audio messages without a legal process, and by request. Moscow at night (Credit: Evgenit/Pixabay) Multiple firms and apps are already on this same list, including WhatsApp and Telegram, so it's not clear why it has taken until now for Apple to be added. It's a continuation of the country's moves to control users' messages, though, as it follows Russia's blocking of FaceTime in 2025. According to Bloomberg, Apple and Microsoft were added to this registry of "organizers of information dissemination" on October 2, 2026. The registry is operated by the country's state media watchdog, Roskomnadzor, which previously forced Apple to remove VPN apps from the App Store. articles.title: Apple MacBook Pro Gets Touchscreen For The First Time, With An Eye-Watering Price Tag
articles.description: Apple has introduced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, bringing touch controls to its professional laptop lineup alongside a new tandem OLED display and M5 Pro and M5 Max processors. The new models are available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes and feature Dynamic Island, enhanced display technology and up to 24 hours of battery life. The new MacBook Pro models are designed for professionals, developers and content creators who need high-performance computing for demanding workloads. Apple has also redesigned the laptops to make them thinner and lighter than their non-touchscreen counterparts. Apple MacBook Pro Touchscreen Models: Price In India Apple's new touchscreen MacBook Pro lineup starts at Rs 3,49,900 in India for the 14-inch model with the M5 Pro chip. The 16-inch version with the same processor is priced at Rs 4,09,900. For users who need more processing and graphics performance, the M5 Max configurations are also available. The 14-inch model with the M5 Max chip costs Rs 5,49,900, while the 16-inch variant is priced at Rs 5,89,900. Eligible students and educators can access lower prices through Apple's education savings programme. The 14-inch M5 Pro model starts at Rs 3,31,900 with education savings, while the 16-inch variant starts at Rs 3,85,900. MacBook Pro Gets Touchscreen OLED Display The biggest change is the introduction of touchscreen functionality on the MacBook Pro for the first time. The new models feature Apple's tandem OLED-based PROLED XDR display, which supports touch input and offers a variable refresh rate of up to 120Hz. According to Apple, the display reaches up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness and offers a claimed contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1. It also supports both the P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, which could benefit professionals working with photographs, videos and colour-sensitive creative projects. Users can interact directly with onscreen content, including manipulating 3D models and working with supported applications using touch gestures. Apple has also introduced Dynamic Island on the Mac, which can display information related to Spotlight, Live Activities and Siri AI. MacBook Pro Powered By M5 Pro And M5 Max Chips The new touchscreen MacBook Pro is available with Apple's M5 Pro and M5 Max processors. Both chip options are designed to handle demanding workloads, including software development, video editing, graphics-intensive applications and artificial intelligence tasks. The laptops support up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage in selected M5 Max configurations. They also feature Thunderbolt 5 connectivity and Apple's latest software platform, macOS 27, with Apple Intelligence capabilities. The M5 Pro configurations are aimed at professionals who need high performance for everyday professional workloads, while the M5 Max variants are designed for more demanding tasks such as 3D animation, visual effects and advanced video production. Battery Life, Design And Other Features Apple claims that the new touchscreen MacBook Pro models can deliver up to 24 hours of battery life on a single charge. The redesigned laptops are also thinner and lighter than the corresponding non-touchscreen models. Other features include a 12MP Center Stage camera, studio-quality microphones and a six-speaker audio system. Apple says the redesigned speaker system delivers 50% deeper bass than the previous generation. The laptops also support Thunderbolt 5, while the display's 120Hz variable refresh rate is designed to provide smoother scrolling and animations. These features are intended to support professional workflows as well as video calls, media consumption and other everyday tasks. MacBook Pro Touchscreen: Availability In India Apple opened pre-orders for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro models on October 28 through its online store and the Apple Store app in selected markets. According to Apple's India announcement, the new models are scheduled to become available from November 9 through the Apple online store and authorised resellers. Customers can choose between 14-inch and 16-inch models, with M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations available at different price points. The launch marks a major change for Apple's professional laptop lineup by adding touchscreen interaction while retaining the performance-focused MacBook Pro design. However, buyers will need to consider the higher starting price when deciding whether the new display and touch features justify an upgrade.

articles.title: Speed, scale and connectivity have changed the face of Uttar Pradesh: Chief Minister
articles.description: Lucknow: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, through the social media platform ‘X’, apprised the people of the state of the unprecedented expansion of road, rail, metro and air connectivity since 2017. He said, “The mantra of speed, scale and connectivity had changed the face of Uttar Pradesh.”The Chief Minister wrote that road, rail and air connectivity do not merely reduce distances; they also bring convenience, save time and open up new possibilities for prosperity. However, before 2017, the condition of these lifelines of development in Uttar Pradesh was extremely deplorable. The Chief Minister wrote, “Under the able guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the double-engine government had transformed this situation through the mantra of speed, scale and connectivity. Before the BJP’s double-engine government came to power, the state with the largest population in the country had only one and a half expressways. Today, 10 expressways are operational in the state. At that time, air services were limited to a select few cities, but today, with 12 domestic and 5 international airports, the state’s flight is reaching new heights. At that time, not a single city in the state had metro services. In contrast, today, metro services are giving a new pace to life in 7 cities.”The Chief Minister stated, “This transformation was providing farmers’ produce with access to larger markets and creating new opportunities for entrepreneurship. Access to education and employment was becoming easier for young people. Working people were saving time.”He further added, “Tourism was also expanding, thereby providing new strength to the livelihoods of local families. This pace of development was transforming the lives of citizens today, from villages to towns and from towns to cities. Opportunities for every sector, capacity for every enterprise and growing prosperity in the life of every family are the new identity of ‘New Uttar Pradesh’ in ‘New India’.”
